title: Long-Term Care Benefit Eligibility under Asset-Based Long-Term Care Life Insurance
content:
Claims manual — eligibility for long-term care benefits on an Ashgrove CareAssure policy of Asset-Based Long-Term Care Life Insurance.

## Formal rule

The insured is eligible for benefits while chronically ill: unable to perform at least the tier's required number of the recognized activities of daily living without substantial assistance for a period expected to last at least the tier's expected duration, or requiring substantial supervision because of severe cognitive impairment. A claim is approved only on a long-term care claim whose request status is approved, supported by a licensed health care practitioner's certification dated within the tier's certification look-back period before the decision and a plan of care. Benefits are payable for care received after the elimination period: the tier's elimination days of chronic illness, which need not be consecutive if they fall within the tier's accumulation window, satisfied once in the insured's lifetime and counted from the benefit eligibility date. Chronic illness must be recertified at the tier's recertification interval; when recertification is not received, or the insured no longer meets the definition, benefits stop and the claim closes.

The request status, the certification date and the receipt of the plan of care are read from that long-term care claim on the company's record.

## Chronically ill — condition table

| Unable to perform at least the required number of activities without substantial assistance | Expected to last at least the required period | Requires substantial supervision because of severe cognitive impairment | Chronically ill |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | — | Yes |
| — | — | Yes | Yes |
| Yes | No | No | No |
| No | — | No | No |

With the CareAssure measures (two of bathing, continence, dressing, eating, toileting and transferring, expected to last at least 90 days), an insured who needs substantial assistance with bathing and dressing, expected to last six months, is chronically ill; an insured who needs it with bathing alone is not, unless the severe cognitive impairment limb is met.

## Claim approval — what must be on the claim

1. The long-term care claim's request status is approved.
2. A licensed health care practitioner's certification dated within the look-back period before the decision.
3. A plan of care.

When the claim is approved, a policy that is In Force, Paid Up or on the Shortened Benefit period becomes Claim Active, recording the benefit eligibility date (the first day of certified chronic illness), the date the elimination period is satisfied and the date of the practitioner certification.

## Elimination period and recertification — cases (hypothetical dates and days)

- The elimination period is counted from the benefit eligibility date, and benefits are payable for care received after it is satisfied.
- An insured whose elimination period was satisfied on an earlier claim does not serve it again: it is satisfied once in the insured's lifetime.
- With the 12-month recertification interval, chronic illness on a claim certified in April 2026 must be recertified 12 months later; if that recertification is not received, or the insured no longer meets the definition, benefits stop and the claim closes.

On closure the policy returns to In Force where ten-pay premiums remain, with the next installment due date as its paid-to date, and otherwise to Paid Up.
